title: NY State Assembly · District 82
area: The Bronx: Co-op City, Country Club, City Island, Pelham Bay, Schuylerville, Throggs Neck, Edgewater Park, Silver Beach, Locust Point, and Westchester Square

context.text: Incumbent Michael Benedetto (D) defeated Jake Kuhl and Felix Omozusi 62.3% to 24.9% to 12.2% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary.

summary.text: Michael Benedetto is the incumbent Democratic Assembly Member for District 82 in the northeast Bronx, first elected in 2004. A former special-education teacher, he chairs the Assembly's Education Committee.

background.text: Benedetto was born in the Bronx in 1947 and has lived his entire life in the northeast Bronx. He earned a B.A. in History/Education from Iona College (1969) and an M.A. in Social Studies/Education (1971).

He spent 35 years teaching, including as a teacher of mentally and physically disabled children in the New York City public schools starting in 1974, and as coordinator of the special-education unit at P.S. 160 in Co-op City from 1988 until his election to the Assembly in 2004.
In 1981 he founded the Bronx Times Reporter, which became the largest community newspaper in the Bronx, and in 1969 he started the Throggs Neck Community Players community theater group.
He chairs the Assembly's Education Committee as of the 2025-2026 session.

priorities.text: Announced a $250,000 state grant to the NYC Department of Sanitation for anti-dumping surveillance cameras in Pelham Bay, and a $75,000 grant to enhance the Rivers Run Community Garden in Co-op City.

Secured a $350,000 capital grant for the Edgewater Park Volunteer Fire Department to purchase a new fire truck, and funding for security cameras along the East Tremont commercial corridor with the Throggs Neck Business Improvement District.

Co-sponsored legislation with Assembly Member Fernandez aimed at reining in operations at the NYPD's Rodman's Neck firearms range to address quality-of-life concerns in East Bronx coastal communities.

positions.summary: In a 2022 candidate survey, said he voted for gun-safety legislation raising the age for assault weapons, strengthening red flag laws, and closing the 'boyfriend loophole.'
positions.quote: I've voted for gun safety legislation including the recent package of legislation to raise the age on assault weapons, strengthen our red flag laws, and close the "boyfriend loophole" so domestic abusers cannot purchase a firearm.

positions.summary: In a 2022 candidate survey, cited his votes for and co-sponsorship of the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act and the Climate and Community Investment Act.
positions.quote: I'm voted consistently for legislation like the New York's Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act (which I co-sponsored) and I'm a co-sponsoring the Climate and Community Investment Act that will bring billions of dollars for climate projects to our area.

record.text: Chairs the Assembly's Education Committee as of the 2025-2026 session.
Announced a $400,000 state grant to Save the Sound to develop a watershed management plan for the Hutchinson River in the Bronx.
Announced $800,000 in state funding for the NYPD to acquire a specialized tow truck to remove tractor-trailers illegally parked on residential streets in the northeast Bronx.

summary.text: Irene Guanill is a real-estate professional and community advocate running as the Republican, Conservative, and Vote Affordable Party candidate for Assembly District 82.

background.text: Guanill earned a high school diploma from the High School of Fashion Industries and has worked as a real-estate professional (Realtor) for over 20 years.
She says she has 25 years of housing experience and has advocated to protect homeownership for homeowners, tenants, and landlords.
She is endorsed by the Bronx Republican Party, the Bronx Conservative Party, Vote Affordable, and North West Bronx Democrats.

priorities.text: On affordability: "Families are struggling with rising taxes, utility bills, insurance costs, and housing expenses. I will fight for ... legislation that lowers the cost of living, supports homeownership, protects small businesses, and creates opportunities for families to build financial security instead of making it harder to get ahead."

"Safe Neighborhoods and Strong Communities. Every family deserves to feel safe at home, at school, and on our streets. I support our law enforcement officers, stronger schools, responsible development, and policies that protect our neighborhoods while improving the quality of life for residents, seniors, veterans, and small businesses."
"Accountability, Integrity and Service. I am your neighbor — not a career politician. I believe government should be transparent, fiscally responsible, and accountable to the people it serves."
"I support grants for first-time home buyers to empower new generations, and I advocate for no property taxes for our seniors, allowing them to age with dignity and security."

positions.summary: Says she will work with police to ensure they have the tools, training, and support needed to keep the district safe.
positions.quote: We will work with our police to ensure they have the proper tools, training, and support needed to keep The Bronx Assembly 82nd District safe.

researchNotes: Benedetto has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, but his 2022 survey responses (still the most recent he has given) include direct, on-the-record stances on gun laws and climate policy, cited above; several 2022 constituent-funding press releases remain the most recent official record items found for him on nyassembly.gov (searches for 2025-2026 press releases and current sponsored-bill lists did not surface additional citable material; his Ballotpedia sponsored-legislation table is rendered by a third-party widget not accessible to this research process). Guanill completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and has a detailed campaign platform; she stated general priorities on affordability, safety, and homeownership but did not take a clear stance matching most of this guide's fixed issue list beyond policing, so only one Position entry is included for her.
